<a id="live-data-dictionary"></a>
## Data Dictionary

**Live View** is MetaSync's interactive global page inside Confluence — a live, filterable view of your synced org that anyone with space access can open, not just admins. Find it via the Confluence **Apps** menu. Unlike the published documentation pages, Live View is rendered on demand and always reflects your **last sync**. It has five tabs — Data Dictionary, Documentation Coverage, Setup Audit Trail, [Flow Visualizer](#live-flows) and [ERD](#live-erd); this is the first.

> **Note — Who can see Live View data.** Live View's data is gated **server-side on Confluence access**: every tab's data call checks — as the viewing user — that they can see the space/page the macro sits on, so Confluence's own permission model decides. Viewers without access to that space get a single informational panel (with a **Retry**) instead of data. Calls that arrive without a page context (e.g. from the MetaSync dashboard) fall back to the admin / granted-access rule from [Additional access](feature-guides.md#feature-connections).

> **Warning — Each viewer sees a one-time "Allow access" prompt.** Because that check runs **as the viewing user**, Atlassian asks each person for consent the first time they open Live View — a one-time **Allow access** dialog naming MetaSync. Accepting it is what lets MetaSync confirm what they're allowed to see; it grants MetaSync nothing beyond that check. A viewer who **declines or dismisses** it gets the access panel instead of data, and the decision sticks for the session: reload the page, accept the prompt, then use **Retry**. If the prompt doesn't reappear, ask the viewer to reload in a new tab. See [Live View: "You don't have access to this data"](troubleshooting.md#ts-live-view-access).

The **Data Dictionary** tab is a cross-object index of every field in your org, flattened into one searchable table. It's built from the field index MetaSync accumulates during sync, so it stays small and fast.

> **Note.** A banner above the table reads `N fields across M objects · last synced <date>`, confirming the freshness of the data. Live View reflects the most recent sync — run a sync to refresh it. See [How syncing works](concepts.md#how-syncing-works).

### The columns

- **Object** — The object's label, with its API name shown underneath in monospace.
- **Field** — The field's label.
- **API name** — The field's API name, in monospace.
- **Type** — The field's data type (Text, Picklist, Lookup, etc.).
- **Req** — A ✓ if the field is required, otherwise a dash.
- **PII** — A **High** or **Medium** badge if the field is classified as personally identifiable, otherwise a dash. Drawn from Salesforce Data Classification — see [PII & data classification](concepts.md#pii-classification).
- **Enc** — An **Enc** badge if the field is encrypted, otherwise a dash.
- **Source** — **Custom** or **Standard** — whether the field is custom-built or a standard/managed-package field.
- **Doc** — **Yes** (green) if the field has a description or help text, **No** (amber) if it has neither.

### Searching and filtering

- **Search box** — matches across object API name, object label, field API name and field label.
- **All objects** dropdown — restrict to one object.
- **All types** dropdown — restrict to one field type.
- **PII only** checkbox — show only fields classified as PII.
- **Encrypted** checkbox — show only encrypted fields.
- A live `N matches` counter sits at the right of the controls.

> **Warning — Display cap.** The table renders up to **1000 matching rows** on screen at once; when more match, the counter reads `(showing 1000)`. Narrow with the filters or the search box to reach fields beyond the cap. (There is no per-object expand/collapse — every field is a flat row.) See [Truncation & display limits](concepts.md#truncation-limits).

> **Note.** If the table is empty it means no fields are indexed yet: run a MetaSync sync with **Objects** enabled, then reload. See [Metadata Types & scope](feature-guides.md#feature-metadata-types).

> **Warning — An empty state is never a disguised failure.** Every Live View tab distinguishes "nothing stored yet" from "we couldn't read it". If the underlying read fails, the tab shows a red **Error: …** line instead of the empty state. That matters because Live View is usually opened by non-admins, who can't run a sync — telling them to "run a sync" when the real problem is a storage read failure would send them down a dead end. A **permission** decision is different again, and is shown once for the whole macro as the informational access panel above — never as a red error on each tab.

<a id="live-coverage"></a>
## Documentation Coverage

The **Documentation Coverage** tab of [Live View](#live-data-dictionary) scores how well your Salesforce schema is documented, on a 0–100 scale, and shows exactly which objects are dragging the score down. Like the rest of Live View it reflects your last sync.

### The composite score

A large **0–100** score sits at the top. It's a weighted composite of three of the metric rows below — **documented fields** count double the others:

*Coverage formula (from computeCoverage in src/features/data-dictionary.ts)*

```
overallScore = round( pctDocumented × 0.5  +  pctHelpText × 0.25  +  scoreSensitiveClassified × 0.25 )
```

Where `pctDocumented` is the share of fields with **a description or help text**, `pctHelpText` the share with help text, and `scoreSensitiveClassified` is the **Detected-sensitive fields classified** row — *not* the *Fields PII / sensitivity classified* row. All are whole-number percentages.

> **Warning — The third term is the detected-sensitive row, not the PII-classified row.** These two metric rows are both shown on the page and they usually differ, because they have different denominators: **Fields PII / sensitivity classified** is measured against *every* field, while **Detected-sensitive fields classified** is measured only against the fields MetaSync's detector flagged as sensitive. The score uses the *detected-sensitive* one. Substituting the PII-classified row into the formula above will not reproduce the score you see.

> **Note — An org with no detected-sensitive fields scores full marks on that term.** When the detector finds **no** sensitive fields at all, `scoreSensitiveClassified` is **100**, not 0 — an org with nothing to classify carries no classification debt and is not docked for it. That contributes the full 25 points. This is why a schema with no PII can still score respectably while showing `0%` on the PII-classified row.

### Colour thresholds

Every percentage badge and progress bar is colour-coded so weak areas jump out:

| Percentage | Colour |
| --- | --- |
| **80% or above** | Green |
| **50–79%** | Amber |
| **Below 50%** | Red |

### The metric rows

- **Fields with descriptions** — Fields that have a description set, out of all fields.
- **Fields with help text** — Fields that have help text, out of all fields. (Weighted 25% of the score.)
- **Fields documented (desc or help)** — Fields with either a description or help text. (Weighted 50% — the heaviest.)
- **Fields PII / sensitivity classified** — Fields with a security classification or compliance group set, out of **all** fields. (Shown for context; **not** the term used in the score.)
- **Detected-sensitive fields classified** — Of the fields MetaSync's detector flagged as sensitive, the share carrying a Salesforce classification. (Weighted 25% — this is the score's third term. Scores 100 when nothing was detected.)
- **Objects fully documented** — Objects where every field is documented, out of all objects. (Shown for context; not part of the score.)

### Least-documented objects

Below the metrics, a **Least-documented objects** table lists up to the 10 worst objects (ascending by documented %), each with its label and API name, a documented-% badge, and a `documented / total` field count — your prioritised to-do list.

### How to improve the score

1. Start with the objects in the **Least-documented** table — fixing the worst objects moves the score fastest.
2. In Salesforce Setup, add **field descriptions and help text** to fields that lack them (documented fields are weighted 50%).
3. **Classify the fields MetaSync detected as sensitive** using Salesforce Data Classification (Security Classification and Compliance Group). Classifying a *detected-sensitive* field is what moves the score's third term — classifying an unflagged field changes the PII-classified row but not the score. See [PII & data classification](concepts.md#pii-classification).
4. Run a MetaSync sync, then reopen this tab — the score refreshes from the new index.

> **Note.** An empty state (`No fields indexed yet`) means you need to run a sync with Objects enabled first. For a downloadable, per-object version of this analysis with a to-document checklist, see the [Documentation Coverage report](reports-reference.md#report-doc-coverage) in Governance.

> **Warning — This score and the Governance report's score are computed differently.** Governance also publishes a 0–100 [Documentation Coverage](reports-reference.md#report-doc-coverage) figure, and **the two numbers will not match** — deliberately. This page scores the *field-documentation* surface (documented %, help text, detected-sensitive classification). The governance report additionally weighs **object descriptions** and uses its own weights, stated in that report's own Summary. Neither is wrong; they answer slightly different questions. Quote whichever you use **with its formula**, and don't reconcile one against the other.

<a id="live-timeline"></a>
## Setup Audit Trail

The **Setup Audit Trail** tab of [Live View](#live-data-dictionary) is a browsable log of configuration changes in your Salesforce org, drawn from the Salesforce **Setup Audit Trail** and captured on each sync. It reflects the most recent sync.

> **Warning — Configuration changes only.** The Setup Audit Trail records **configuration changes** (who changed which setting) — **not record data changes**. And Salesforce only retains it for about **180 days**, so the timeline is a rolling window. A banner states this: `N changes from the Setup Audit Trail (config changes only, not record data; Salesforce retains ~180 days)`. To keep audit history beyond that window, use the [Change History report](reports-reference.md#report-change-history) in Governance.

### The columns

- **When** — The date and time the change was made.
- **User** — The user who made the change; if performed on behalf of someone, a `via <delegate>` note appears underneath.
- **Type** — A colour-coded badge derived from the action: **Created** (green), **Changed** (blue), **Deleted** (red), or **Other** (grey).
- **Section** — The Setup area the change occurred in (or a dash).
- **Detail** — The human-readable description of what changed.

### Filters

- **Search box** — matches across the detail, section, user and action text.
- **All users** dropdown — filter to changes made by a single user.
- **All change types** dropdown — filter by **Created**, **Changed**, **Deleted**, or **Other**.
- A live `N matches` counter sits at the right of the controls.

> **Note.** If the timeline is empty (`No change history stored yet`), run a MetaSync sync with **Setup Audit Trail** enabled in [Metadata types](feature-guides.md#feature-metadata-types), then reload.

<a id="live-flows"></a>
## Flow Visualizer

The **Flow Visualizer** tab of [Live View](#live-data-dictionary) draws each of your Salesforce Flows as a diagram, in the style of Flow Builder. Pick a flow from the dropdown (grouped into **Active** and **Inactive**, with an element count beside each) to render its canvas. It reflects your last sync.

### Reading the diagram

Each element is drawn as a **Salesforce-style shape**, colour-coded by type, so the flow's structure is readable at a glance:

- **Diamond** — **Decision** and **Wait** elements — the branching points. Each outgoing path is labelled with its outcome.
- **Hexagon** — **Loop** elements — with `for each` and `after last` paths.
- **Rectangle** — **Screen** and data elements (**Record Create / Update / Delete / Lookup**).
- **Rounded rectangle** — **Actions**, **Apex**, **Subflows**, **Assignments** and other elements.
- **Green Start** — The synthetic start node the flow runs from.

Connectors are colour-coded too: normal paths are grey, decision outcomes orange, fault paths red (dashed), and loop paths magenta. **Click any element** to open a side panel with its description, configuration detail, and — for decisions — each outcome's conditions (`field operator value`).

### Flow type, entry criteria and variables

- A **type badge** next to the picker shows how the flow runs — **Record-Triggered** (with before/after save and the create/update timing), **Scheduled**, **Screen Flow**, **Platform Event**, or **Autolaunched** — plus the trigger object.
- **Entry criteria** — for record-triggered flows, the conditions under which the flow runs are shown above the diagram (`field operator value`, joined by the flow's AND/OR logic).
- **Variables** — an expandable list of the flow's declared variables with their data type and whether each is a collection, input or output.

> **Note.** The same diagram (shapes, type badge, entry criteria and variables) is also embedded on each Flow's **published documentation page**, rendered as an image. If the Flow Visualizer is empty, run a MetaSync sync with **Flows** enabled in [Metadata types](feature-guides.md#feature-metadata-types), then reload.

<a id="live-erd"></a>
## ERD

The **ERD** (Entity Relationship Diagram) tab of [Live View](#live-data-dictionary) shows how your objects relate to one another. Each box is an object; each arrow points from the object holding a **lookup or master-detail field** to the object it references, labelled with the field(s) backing the relationship. It reflects your last sync.

Relationships are derived from the object dependency graph MetaSync builds during sync — the same data behind [Change Impact](feature-guides.md#feature-change-impact) — so the diagram stays consistent with the rest of your documentation. Self-referencing hierarchies (an object looking up to itself) are omitted to keep the diagram readable.

> **Note.** A companion **Entity Relationship Diagram** page is also published into your Confluence space (under the home page), with the diagram as an image plus a full relationship table for large orgs. If the ERD is empty, run a MetaSync sync with **Objects** enabled, then reload.
